The operator for spin along a unit vector  

 n = (sin θ, 0, cos θ)  ( n lies in the x–z plane, azimuthal angle φ = 0 )

is  

 P_n = n·P = (ħ/2)(sin θ σ_x + cos θ σ_z)

so, after dividing by ħ/2, the matrix whose eigenvectors we want is  

 M = sin θ σ_x + cos θ σ_z  
   = sin θ [[0,1],[1,0]] + cos θ [[1,0],[0,−1]]  
   = [[cos θ,  sin θ],  
     sin θ, −cos θ]].

For the eigenvalue +1 (which corresponds to the physical eigenvalue +ħ/2),
let v = (a, b)ᵀ.  Then

 [[cos θ, sin θ],[sin θ,−cos θ]]·(a,b)ᵀ = (a,b)ᵀ

gives the simultaneous equations  
 (cos θ − 1)a + sin θ b = 0  
 sin θ a − (cos θ + 1)b = 0.

From the first, b = [(1 − cos θ)/sin θ] a = tan(θ/2) a.

Choosing the convenient (and already normalized) scale a = cos(θ/2) then yields  
 b = sin(θ/2).

Hence the normalized eigenvector is

 |+; n⟩ = (cos (θ/2), sin (θ/2))ᵀ.

This matches option (B).

Answer: B
